2. Protium, Deuterium and Tritium are isotopes of carbon.
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
Code :
x: Statement 1 is correct. Atoms of the same element having the same atomic number (number of protons) but different mass number (due to different number of neutrons) are called isotopes. Therefore, their chemical properties are generally similar, while some physical properties (e.g., mass, stability) may differ. Examples: Oxygen-16, Oxygen-17 and Oxygen-18; Chlorine-35 and Chlorine-37, etc. Statement 2 is incorrect. Protium (1H1), Deuterium (2H1) and Tritium (3H1) are isotopes of hydrogen, not carbon. The main isotopes of carbon are Carbon-12, Carbon-13 and Carbon-14.

s: The difference between a nuclear reactor and an atomic bomb is that
o: no chain reaction takes place in nuclear reactor

x: A nuclear reactor sustains a fission chain reaction in a controlled manner, regulating the rate of energy release through moderators and control rods that absorb neutrons. It relies on delayed neutrons and built-in safety systems to maintain stable, steady power generation. In contrast, an atomic (fission) bomb is designed for an uncontrolled, rapid chain reaction, achieving a supercritical state that releases enormous energy within a fraction of a second, without mechanisms to regulate or moderate the reaction.

s:
Consider the following statements: In a nuclear reactor, self-sustained chain reaction is possible, because
I. more neutrons are released in each of the fission reactions.
II. the neutrons immediately take part in the fission process. Science and Technology PMF IAS S&T – 56
III. the fast neutrons are slowed down by Graphite.
IV. every neutron released in the fission reaction initiates further fission. Which of these statements are correct?
x: In a nuclear reactor, a self-sustained chain reaction is possible because each fission reaction releases additional neutrons, making Statement I correct. These neutrons are initially fast-moving and are slowed down by moderators such as Graphite to increase the probability of further fission, so Statement III is also correct. Statement II is incorrect because neutrons do not immediately take part in fission; they usually need to be slowed down first. Statement IV is also incorrect because not every neutron released causes another fission—some may escape or get absorbed without producing further reactions.

s: Consider the following statements about nuclear fusion reactors : i. They work on the principle of fission of heavy nuclei. ii. They usually have Tokamak design. iii. They operate at very high temperature. Of these

Only ii and iii are correct
All the three i, ii and iii are correct
x: Nuclear fusion reactors work on the principle of fusion of two light nuclei. So, statement (i) is incorrect. Nuclear fusion reactions are also called ‘Thermonuclear reactions’ because they operate at very high temperature. Usually, nuclear fusion reactors have Tokamak design.

Consider the following statements.

s: The alpha particle carries two positive charges. Its mass is very nearly equal to that of –
o: Nucleus of an atom of helium
Sum of masses of two positrons and two neutrons
Two positrons, as each positron carries a single
x: An alpha particle is a fast moving particle containing two protons and two neutrons (a helium nucleus). Its mass is equal to that of helium atom's nucleus. Alpha particles carry a charge of +2 and strongly interact with matter.

s:
With reference to the radioactivity, which of the following statements is/are correct ?
1. Radioactivity is a nuclear property.
2. Hydrogen bomb is prepared on the principle of nuclear fission.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
Codes :
x: Radioactivity is a nuclear phenomenon in which an unstable atomic nucleus undergoes a decay. In this process, unstable atomic nucleus loses energy by radiation. It is the process of spontaneous emission of alpha, beta and gamma radiations from the nuclei of an atom. Hence, statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect as hydrogen bomb is prepared on the principle of nuclear fusion in which nuclei of isotopes of hydrogen combine under extremely high temperature to form helium nucleus.

s: Which particle is free of charge?
x: Among the given particles neutron is free of charge. α (alpha) particle (+2ve) and proton (+ve) are positive charged particles while electron (–ve) carries negative charge.

s: Radioactivity is measured by –
x: The Geiger–Muller Counter also called a Geiger Counter, is an instrument used for detection and measurement of ionizing radiation. It detects radiation such as alpha particles, beta particles and gamma rays using the ionization produced in a Geiger-Muller tube, which gives its name to the instrument.

s: Which among the following is a positively charged particle emitted by a radioactive element?
o: More than one of the above
x: Alpha rays or Alpha particles (α) are the positively charged particles emitted by a radioactive element. These are nuclei of helium (2He4++). Its mass is equal to the atomic mass of nucleus of helium atom.

s: Which of the following is not a radio active element?
x: Zirconium (Z = 40) is not radioactive, whereas elements above Z 80 are mostly radioactive. Astatine and francium are heavy radioactive elements, and tritium is a radioactive hydrogen isotope.

s: Beta rays emitted by a radioactive material are
o: the electrons orbiting around the nucleus.
x: Beta rays are electrons (negative beta) or positrons (positive beta) emitted from the nucleus, so they are charged particles. They are not neutral and not electromagnetic radiation (that is gamma).

s: Half-life of a radioactive element is 10 days. What does it mean?
o: Element will be completely disintigrate in 20 days.
Element will be completely disintigrate in 40 days.
3/4th part of element will disintigrate in 20 days.
1/4th part of element will distintigarate in 5 days.
x: After one half-life (10 days) half remains; after two (20 days) a quarter remains, so 3/4 has decayed. The element never fully disintegrates, so options 1 and 2 are wrong.

s: In an observation, α-particles, β-particles and γ-rays have same energies. Their penetrating power in a given medium in increasing order will be
x: Alpha is stopped by paper, beta by a few mm of aluminium, and gamma only by lead or concrete. Penetrating power therefore increases in the order alpha, beta, gamma.

s: What is the function of moderator in a nuclear reactor?
What happens if the control rods are not used in a nuclear reactor?
o: Chain process would go out of bounds
The reactor will be slow to act
The reactor will continue to work as it is
x: Control rod constitutes a real-time control of fission process which is crucial for both keeping the fission chain reaction active and preventing it from accelerating beyond control. These rods are composed of chemical elements such as boron, silver, indium and cadmium.

s: The substance used as moderator and coolant both, in nuclear reactors is :
Heavy water is a type of –
x: Heavy water (D₂O) is used chiefly as a moderator to slow neutrons in nuclear reactors.

s: Gas cooled reactor uses following materials as moderator and coolant.
x: A gas-cooled reactor uses graphite as the moderator and carbon dioxide gas as the coolant. The notes do not cover this reactor type.

s: Heavy water is used as a moderator in a nuclear reactor. The function of the moderator is
o: to control the energy released in the reactor.
to absorb neutrons and stop the chain reaction.
to slow down the neutrons to thermal energy.
x: A moderator slows fast neutrons so that U-235 can fission. Absorbing neutrons and controlling the rate is the job of the control rods.

s: If control rods are not used in the nuclear reactor, then
o: chain reaction will go out of control.
there will be impact on nuclear reactor.
x: Control rods absorb neutrons and regulate the reaction rate. Without them the chain reaction goes out of bounds, so it would not stop or slow down.

s: The function of heavy water in a nuclear reactor is to?
o: Slow down the speed of neutrons.
x: Heavy water (D₂O) primarily acts as a moderator in certain nuclear reactors. During nuclear fission, fast neutrons are released, but these neutrons are less effective at sustaining a chain reaction. Heavy water slows down these neutrons to thermal energies without absorbing many of them, thereby increasing the likelihood of further fission in fuel such as natural uranium. Although heavy water can also serve as a coolant in some reactor designs, its principal function is neutron moderation.

s: The function of heavy water in a nuclear reactor is to
o: Slow down the speed of neutrons
x: Heavy water (D2O), also called deuterium oxide, contains a larger than normal amount of the hydrogen isotope deuterium (1H2). It is used as moderator in the reactor to slow down the neutrons produced in fission so that the chain reaction can be sustained. Many reactors also use Light water or normal water (H2O), Graphite or Beryllium oxide as moderator. In India, mainly heavy water is used as moderator in nuclear reactors.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding Fast Breeder Reactors:

I. Fast Breeder Reactors are designed to breed more fuel than they consume.

II. In this reactor, Plutonium-239 undergoes fission to produce energy, while the Uranium-238 present in the fuel transmutes to additional Plutonium-239.

III. It is a part of stage I of India's Nuclear power programme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: A fast breeder reactor breeds more fissile material than it burns, as U-238 is converted to Pu-239. It is Stage II of the programme, not Stage I, so statement III is wrong.

s:
To meet its rapidly growing energy demand, some opinion that india should pursue research and development on thorium as the future fuel of nuclear energy. In this context, what advantage does thorium hold over uranium?

I. Thorium is far more abundant in nature than uranium.

II. On the basis of per unit mass of mined mineral, thorium can generate more energy compared to natural uranium.

III. Thorium produces less harmful waste compared to uranium.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Thorium is more abundant than uranium, gives more energy per unit mass mined, and produces less harmful waste. All three statements are therefore correct.

s: Which company is building the first Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) in India?
India's indigenous Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) of 500 MWe capacity at Kalapakkam was developed by:
o: Central Institute of Mining and Fuel Research (CIMFR)
Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR)
x: The PFBR was designed by IGCAR but built and commissioned by BHAVINI. The question asks who developed it, and the key is BHAVINI.

s: Which one of the following coolants is used in the ‘Fast Breeder Test Reactor’ at Kalpakkam ?
x: Fast Breeder Test Reactor (FBTR) at Kalpakkam is being operated on experimental basis since 1985. It uses uranium and plutonium mixed carbide fuel. FBTR uses liquid sodium as coolant, which is reactive with air or water. The reactor uses a coolant that removes heat from the core where the fuel is processed and carry it to an electrical generator. Coolant also serves to maintain manageable pressures within the core.

s: A breeder reactor is that which –
o: Does not require fissionable material at all
Produces more fissionable material than it burns
x: A breeder reactor produces more fissile material than it burns. Fast neutrons convert the fertile U-238 blanket into Pu-239.

s: The Indira Gandhi Atomic Research Centre is located in :
x: Kalpakkam (Chennai, Tamil Nadu) is known for its nuclear plants and affiliated research installations. These include the Madras Atomic Power Station (MAPS), a nuclear power plant, and the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR- established in 1971), an affiliate of the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) and the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC). Madras Atomic Power Station (MAPS) is a comprehensive nuclear power production, fuel reprocessing, and waste treatment facility that includes plutonium fuel fabrication for fast breeder reactors (FBRs). It is also India's first fully indigenously constructed nuclear power station, with two units each generating 220 MWe of electricity (operated by NPCIL). Kalpakkam is also home to India's first large scale fast breeder reactor of 500 MWe (under construction) called the Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor operated by BHAVINI and will also be the site of first two FBR-600 commercial fast breeder reactors. A beachhead at Kalpakkam also hosts India's first indigenous pressurised (light) water reactor (PWR). The 80 MWe reactor was developed by Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) as the land-based prototype of the nuclear power unit for India's nuclear submarines.

s: The fuel used in Fast Breeder Test Reactor at Kalpakkam is :
x: This reactor's design is based on the French reactor Rhapsody, with several modifications. It uses plutonium-uranium carbide developed indigenously as the driver fuel and went critical on 18 October, 1985.

s: Fast Breeder Reactor is a nuclear reactor which produces energy with the
o: using hard water as a fuel
x: A fast breeder reactor generates electricity by nuclear fission, while its fertile blanket breeds more fissile material. It does not use solar cells, fossil burning or hard water as fuel.

s: In Fast Breeder Reactor of Kalpakkam which of the following is used as a coolant?
x: Fast breeder reactors, including the FBTR at Kalpakkam, use liquid sodium as the coolant and have no moderator.
